text:
The Florida Panthers' three-game winning streak ended in Ottawa, where the Senators turned a one-goal first period into a 5-1 rout. Brady Tkachuk gave FLA the lead on a power play at 10:00, but Tim Stützle answered on the man advantage just over four minutes later, and OTT scored four more over the final two periods without allowing another.

The result was lopsided, but the play was closer than the score. OTT had the better of the chances, with an expected goals total (a measure of the quality of the shots each side took) of 2.34 to 1.65, and out-attempted FLA 50 to 42. By deserved to win, which asks how often a team comes out ahead if every shot were replayed many times, OTT rates at 64 percent and FLA at 36. That is an edge, not a blowout. Two of the goals came on low-probability looks: Claude Giroux scored the go-ahead goal on a 4 percent chance, and Shane Pinto added another from a 5 percent chance late in the second. Akira Schmid allowed 2.7 goals more than his 30 shots against deserved, while Linus Ullmark stopped 17 of 18 for OTT after Samuel Ersson faced one shot.

Stephen Halliday had a goal and an assist, and Stützle and Jake Sanderson (two assists) led the way in the stars. Warren Foegele and Halliday scored in the third to put it away. The loss ends FLA's streak at three games, while OTT adds a home win and some belief that its scoring can arrive even when the chances are close.
